transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having a hard time staying on what I’m doing. For the past year or so, even small things—like my phone buzzing, someone walking past my office, or just some random thought popping into my head—can pull me off task before I even realize it. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should come in.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah, I do. When I’m supposed to sit still—like at a family dinner or a church volunteer meeting—I feel like there’s a motor running inside me. I’ll start moving around or messing with something in my hands because just sitting there feels hard.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah, I do. I’ll jump in before I really think about it—like cutting into my wife’s conversations with her parents, or finishing an employee’s thought before they’re even done talking. I don’t mean to be rude, but I can tell it rubs people the wrong way.
Have you had difficulty completing tasks or assignments at work or school?

Yeah, at work mostly. I’ll start a planning document or sit down with one of my managers, and I’m with it for the first few minutes. But then I’ll realize I’ve missed a good chunk of what they said, and I have to ask them to go back over it. It makes finishing things take longer than it should.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I get frustrated like anyone else, but I haven’t really noticed a big problem with losing control of my emotions.
Were you more active or restless than your peers when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. Looking back, even as a kid, teachers were always moving my seat because I talked too much, or I’d get up without asking. I remember blurting out answers before they even finished the question.
Have you experienced these difficulties with attention and impulsivity your whole life, or did they start more recently?

I think it’s been there most of my life. Looking back, it was happening when I was a kid too—teachers would move my seat because I talked too much, or I’d get up without asking. I’d also blurt things out before they finished the question.
Have these difficulties with attention and impulsivity caused you significant problems or distress in your daily life?

Yeah, I’d say it has, though I’m still functioning overall. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but it does cause problems. At home, I can tell it’s starting to affect trust when family plans don’t go the way they should. And at work, people seem to have less patience with me when meetings or mentoring conversations get off track. So… yes, it’s causing some strain.
Have you experienced these difficulties with attention and impulsivity consistently throughout your childhood and into adulthood?

Yes. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t something that just started recently. When I was a kid, teachers were always moving my seat because I talked too much, or I’d get up without asking. I’d blurt things out before they even finished the question. So yeah, it’s been pretty consistent.
Do you think your difficulties are more with staying focused and paying attention, or with being restless and impulsive, or is it kind of an equal mix of both?

I’d say it’s more the restless and impulsive side. Like when I’m supposed to just sit still—family dinners, or church volunteer meetings—it feels like there’s a motor running in me. I need to move around or at least do something with my hands.
Did you have more energy or fidget more than your peers when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. Even now it shows up—like in meetings I’m usually bouncing my knee, clicking a pen, or shifting around in the chair. People sometimes give me looks like I’m trying to rush them, even when I’m really trying to listen. So as a kid, yeah, I was probably more fidgety than most.
Have you ever lost a job, had relationship problems, or experienced other significant life difficulties because of your restlessness, impulsivity, or difficulty staying focused?

I haven’t lost a job or anything like that. I’m still keeping up overall. But it is starting to cause problems. At home, it’s costing me some trust when family plans don’t go the way they should. And at work, people can lose patience with me in meetings or mentoring conversations when I’m too restless or jump in too quickly. So it’s not ruining everything, but it is affecting things.
Have your symptoms ever caused you significant problems at work or in your personal relationships?

Yeah, I mean, I’m still keeping up overall, but it has caused some problems. At home it’s starting to cost me trust when family plans don’t go how they’re supposed to. And at work, people can get impatient with me in meetings or mentoring conversations when things don’t go smoothly. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but it is affecting both areas.
Have you ever felt like your symptoms have significantly impaired your ability to function at work or in social situations?

Yeah, I’d say it’s starting to, but not to the point where I can’t function. I’m still keeping up overall. It’s more that at home, when family plans don’t go the way they should, it costs me trust. And at work, in meetings or mentoring conversations, people can lose patience with me. So it’s not completely stopping me, but it is definitely affecting things.
Do you often feel excessively fidgety or restless when you're sitting still as an adult?

Yes, pretty often. If I’m supposed to sit still, like at a family dinner or a church volunteer meeting, I feel like there’s a motor running in me. I’ll want to shift around or do something with my hands. It’s hard to just sit calmly.
Do you think your difficulties are more with staying focused, more with being restless and impulsive, or is it about an equal mix of both?

I think it’s more the restless side for me. Like I was saying, when I’m supposed to sit still at a family dinner or a church volunteer meeting, I just feel like there’s a motor running in me. I need to move around or do something with my hands.
Have your symptoms ever caused you to have significant difficulty with social relationships or at your job?

Yeah, it has caused some difficulty. I’m still keeping up overall, but at home it can cost me trust when family plans don’t go the way they should. And at work, in meetings or mentoring conversations, people can get impatient with me. So it’s not like I’m failing at everything, but it is starting to affect those relationships.
Were you often described as hyperactive when you were a child?
Yeah, I was. Looking back, teachers were always moving my seat because I talked too much, or I’d get up without asking. I’d also blurt out answers before they even finished the question sometimes.
Have you ever had any periods in your life where your symptoms were completely under control?

I don’t think they’ve ever been completely under control, no. But it’s been noticeably harder to manage for about a year and a couple months now, since the conflict with my in-laws started taking up more of our family life.
Would you describe your symptoms as mild, moderate, or severe in terms of how much they interfere with your daily life?

I’d call it mild, I think. I’m still functioning and keeping up overall, but it does create problems. Like at home, if family plans don’t go the way they should, it can cost me trust. And at work, people can lose patience with me in meetings or mentoring conversations. So it’s not ruining my life, but it’s definitely interfering some.
